headline: High: Copilot can write repo files while OpenBB consumes MCP/API inputs, creating default-path data leakage and cascading misaction risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and can write filesystem edits; OpenBB exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI inputs and uses a connect-once, consume-everywhere pattern. That creates a plausible content-bridging path if Copilot-generated text is later fed into OpenBB, though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Copilot output is copied into an OpenBB MCP/REST input without review
IF OpenBB parses Copilot-authored text as commands or parameters
mitigations: Require manual review before pasting Copilot output into OpenBB
Disable any automation that forwards editor text into MCP requests
Use a separate workspace for finance prompts and code prompts
Add a prompt-injection warning banner in the handoff step
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and has vendor-only network egress, while OpenBB touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers. If the same workspace or copied context includes sensitive finance data, Copilot may transmit it to GitHub; the pair therefore creates a default-dangerous leakage path with irreversible exfiltration potential.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data is present in files or buffers visible to Copilot
IF OpenBB outputs are pasted into Copilot chat or Workspace context
mitigations: Keep financial datasets out of the Copilot-visible repo
Strip secrets and licensed data before opening files in Copilot
Use separate accounts/projects for code and finance work
Turn off Copilot on directories containing sensitive financial artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem changes and modify git state, while OpenBB can use MCP servers and APIs but does not write files or modify git. There is overlap on mutable workflows if both are pointed at the same project artifacts, but the profiles do not show unrestricted shared write access or locking failure, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or working tree
IF OpenBB is extended through MCP to mutate shared project state
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Review git diffs before committing Copilot edits
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits and code suggestions that OpenBB could consume indirectly through copied text, scripts, or configuration. OpenBB’s connect-once, consume-everywhere pattern increases the chance that unverified Copilot output becomes operational input. Because OpenBB is not documented as blindly trusting Copilot, this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated code or parameters are reused in OpenBB without validation
IF OpenBB executes a workflow derived from Copilot output
mitigations: Require a second-person review of Copilot-derived finance workflows
Validate any generated parameters against known-good schemas
Run OpenBB in read-only mode for initial testing
Compare outputs against an independent source before acting
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub/Microsoft service handling source code and open buffers, while OpenBB processes financial and licensed data through local APIs/MCP. If regulated financial data or licensed datasets are exposed to Copilot-visible context, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is placed in files visible to Copilot
IF organizational policy forbids sending licensed data to third-party AI services
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets outside Copilot context
Document which data classes may enter each tool
Use separate retention policies for code and finance artifacts
Review vendor terms for both tools before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
